title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The document outlines the AI Office's recent decision regarding the implementation of new AI guidelines and regulatory measures. It explains the rationale behind the decision and outlines the expected impacts on stakeholders and future AI development.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The document outlines the process and requirements for filling a vacancy for technology specialists in AI within the AI office. It describes the qualifications, responsibilities, and expectations for potential candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces an opening for a Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI office. The position involves guiding research strategy and ensuring scientific integrity of AI projects.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy introduces a new AI‑enabled legal officer role designed to assist legal teams with contract review, regulatory compliance, and risk assessment. It outlines the duties, required qualifications, and guidelines for integrating AI tools into daily legal operations.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy explains how to fill vacant AI policy officer roles, detailing who qualifies and how they are chosen. It also outlines the duties of those officers so they can manage and oversee AI policy effectively.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing the European Union’s AI Act. They examine the act’s legal, technical, and ethical implications and advise policymakers on how to strengthen regulation and ensure safe, responsible AI deployment.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document is a preliminary request for creating standard guidelines related to AI policy and practice. It seeks to outline common principles and procedures that could be adopted by organizations to ensure consistent and responsible use of AI technologies.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: A “CoP Consultation Notice” is an announcement that opens a public consultation period about a Community of Practice (CoP) policy or guideline. It invites stakeholders to give feedback, explains the main goals and deadlines, and tells people how and where to submit their comments.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This policy invites individuals and organizations to express interest in forming a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI governance. The goal is to bring together diverse stakeholders to collaborate on developing best practices, guidelines, and shared learning around responsible AI.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy explains how a Community of Practice (CoP) uses an iterative drafting process, showing each step from initial idea to final document. It outlines collaboration, feedback loops, and revisions that ensure the policy is thorough, clear, and continually improved.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process is a visual representation that maps out the stages involved in creating the AI policy, highlighting key milestones, dates, and participant roles. It offers a clear, chronological overview of the drafting workflow, allowing stakeholders to see when each phase occurs and how the process unfolds.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document is the first draft of a code of practice that aims to guide organizations in responsibly developing and deploying AI systems, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and accountability. It outlines preliminary principles and recommendations that stakeholders can use as a foundation for establishing safer, ethical AI practices.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document presents the second draft of a Code of Practice, outlining standards and responsibilities for developers, users, and regulators in the AI sector. It aims to promote safe, transparent, and accountable AI practices.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document presents the third draft of a Code of Practice for artificial intelligence, offering a set of guidelines and standards to help developers, users, and regulators promote responsible and ethical AI use. It addresses key areas such as transparency, fairness, safety, accountability, and ongoing compliance so stakeholders can design, deploy, and monitor AI systems in a trustworthy and legally compliant manner.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft outlines a collaborative agreement among stakeholders to guide the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence. It sets shared principles for safety, transparency, and ethical use to help build trust and mitigate risks.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a formal agreement outlining shared principles and commitments to responsible AI development and deployment. It establishes guidelines for safety, transparency, and cooperation among stakeholders to ensure AI technologies are aligned with societal values and human well‑being.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: The policy lists the specific ways that AI should not be used, such as for malicious or deceptive purposes, for creating harmful deepfakes, or in ways that bypass human oversight. It explains why those practices are forbidden and gives guidance to help people avoid them and keep AI use safe and ethical.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This document provides clear rules and criteria for identifying what counts as an AI system. It helps organizations determine which technologies, tools, or processes fall under AI regulations and how they should be categorized.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: The policy outlines strategies to promote start-up growth and foster innovation across the economy. It details communication plans and initiatives designed to support entrepreneurs, encourage new technologies, and build a vibrant innovation ecosystem.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start‑Ups is a European program designed to help new companies harness high‑performance computing. It provides resources, mentorship, and access to advanced computing infrastructure to support innovation and growth in start‑ups.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: A slideshow presentation for a webinar that discusses how to manage risk in AI projects. It covers identifying potential risks, assessing their impact, and outlining strategies to mitigate or govern those risks.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar covers risk management practices relevant to AI, discussing strategies for identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential risks. It provides actionable guidelines for organizations to implement robust risk management frameworks to ensure ethical and safe AI deployment.
